title: Karger's algorithm terminates with two vertices
statement: Let $n \ge 2$, and let $T$ be an adaptive graph trace of $n-2$ steps whose initial multigraph $T_0$ has exactly $n$ vertices. Then the multigraph $T_{n-2}$ reached after all $n-2$ contraction steps is a valid output of the algorithm; that is, it has exactly two vertices.
hypotheses_covered: T is an adaptive graph trace of n−2 steps
the initial graph T₀ has exactly n vertices
replaced:
If $2 \le n$ and an adaptive graph trace of $n-2$ steps starts from a graph with $n$
vertices, then its final graph is a Karger output.
